summary: Del Norte County, CA lookout on Siskiyou NF: a 40-ft timber tower built 1940, later removed; a 2026 amateur-radio site describes remains at the top of a rough trail.

facts.design: 40-foot creosoted sawn timber tower with cab
facts.status_note: Forest Lookouts marks the tower removed; a 2026 amateur-radio site describes remains at the top of a rough trail

visit.trail_note: Reached by a rough, steep road from Smith River and then a short rough trail that the amateur-radio site says needs a 4x4. The sources do not say whether the site is open to the public.

events.note: A 40-foot creosoted sawn timber tower with cab constructed; the page dates the work to a forest history it cites

evidence.supports: built 1940 as a 40-foot creosoted sawn timber tower with cab
evidence.quote: 1940: A 40-foot creosoted sawn timber tower with cab constructed. (A History of the Siskyou National Forest)

evidence.supports: Del Norte County; Siskiyou National Forest
evidence.quote: Del Norte County - Siskiyou National Forest

evidence.supports: listed as Low Divide (Stone Corral), tower, gone, at the FFLA coordinates
evidence.quote: Del Norte Low Divide (Stone Corral) 41.92771 -124.01854 Tower Gone

evidence.supports: listed as a decommissioned fire lookout location
evidence.quote: Stone Corral Lookout is a decomissioned fire lookout location.

evidence.supports: remains at the top of the trail
evidence.quote: 41.92778, -124.01863 : At top of this trail is the remains of Stone Corral Lookout.

evidence.supports: road described as rough and steep
evidence.quote: Road is rough and steep and takes some time to get here.
41.92730, -124.01956 : Turn right onto a short rough trail and go up in 4x4 drive.

corrections.why: The Forest Lookouts page says the tower was removed, but an amateur-radio site describes remains at the top of the trail, so 'gone' understates what is there. The remains claim comes from a hobby-site comment, so an editor should confirm it from another source or on the ground.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The second brief record gives 41.9332, -124.0183, about 0.6 km north of the FFLA point (41.92771, -124.01854). The amateur-radio site gives 41.927773, -124.018631 for the remains, which matches the FFLA point. The record keeps the FFLA coordinates.

notes_for_editor: The 1940 build date and the removed status come from the Forest Lookouts page, which cites A History of the Siskyou National Forest; that book was not opened. The remains and 4x4 access come from a user-comment section on an amateur-radio site and should be checked before publishing. No staffing data in the sources read. The 'Siskyou' spelling is the source's own. The brief's name is Low Divide (Stone Corral); the Forest Lookouts page calls it Stone Corral.
